newsitem.title: CHINA: China to boost exports of value-added goods.
newsitem.headline: China to boost exports of value-added goods.

text.p: China will boost exports of value-added goods, including metallurgical and electrical products, while reducing the export share of traditional items such as garments and textiles, officials said on Wednesday.

"China will expand exports of more value-added products, we have policies to encourage exports," a spokesman of the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation said by telephone without giving details.
China would gradually reduce the share of traditional items such as garments and textiles in exports, he added.
However, the ministry spokesman ruled out any immediate government policies to promote exports in the metallurgy industry.
"They are unlikely to enjoy special preferential policies in the short term," the spokesman said. He declined to give further details.
The Hong Kong-based Ta Kung Pao newspaper has reported that Chinese government ministries are considering measures to promote metallurgical exports.
China would allow more manufacturing firms to conduct foreign trade in future, an official of the State Trade and Economic Commission said. He declined to elaborate.
